name: BC Conservation Fund, Stream 1: Area Based Conservation Initiatives
summary: Grants for non-profits and community contribution companies in British Columbia building community mandate, planning and long-term stewardship and restoration of new conservation areas, with priority for First Nations. Expression of interest first.

amount.note: Phase 1 community initiatives tend to range up to $100K; more complex multi-year projects up to $250K.

reporting: Quarterly check-in calls, annual reports covering progress on deliverables and finances, and an end-of-project report.

steps: Submit a full application, if invited

eligibility.rule: Matching funds exclude provincial government funds
Non-Indigenous applicants show First Nation support
Advance 30x30 via lasting conservation designations meeting IUCN standards
Long-term stewardship: designation after April 1, 2024 and not already counted toward 30x30
Government teams cannot apply directly for their own initiatives or studies
Phase 2 project aligns with a government-to-government land-use agreement
Phase 3 project supports ongoing stewardship of the area
Provide meaningful biological, ecological and cultural benefits and monitor outcomes

documents: Letter or other evidence of First Nation support for non-Indigenous applicants

calls.label: Expressions of interest (rolling)

status.quote: Stream 1 EOI Submissions are always open.

calls.note: Expressions of interest are reviewed in two intakes a year; approved ones are invited to submit a full proposal.

applicant_types.quote: Grants are open to any non-profit organization or community contribution company (C3) working on conservation or land/water use issues in BC. This includes Qualified and Non-Qualified Donee's. For BC Conservation Fund purposes, qualified donees may include: • First Nations • Charities and societies • Non-government organization (NGOs) • Universities and colleges

geography.quote: The BC Conservation Fund is a fund that supports the conservation of biodiverse land and freshwater areas in BC.

access.quote: Before being invited to complete a full funding application for review, an expression of interest must be completed and reviewed by the BC Conservation Fund.

window.quote: Stream 1 EOI Submissions are always open.

amount.quote: We anticipate that for smaller, more community-based initiatives in phase 1, grants will tend to range up to $100K, while more complex, multi-year projects will likely range up to $250K.

reporting.quote: All projects will be asked to meet accountability requirements and provide regular reporting on outcomes. This is accomplished throuhg three types of reports: • Quarterly Check-In's:

effort.quote: Before being invited to complete a full funding application for review, an expression of interest must be completed and reviewed by the BC Conservation Fund.
Application templates will be made available once an Expression of Interest (EOI) has been reviewed and the proponent has been invited to complete the full application.
Projects will be reviewed by the BC Conservation Fund Oversight Committee using a consistent set of criteria and considerations.

eligibility.quote: Please note that provincial government funds are not eligible to be counted as match.
Non-Indigenous organizations can apply where First Nation support is demonstrated (i.e. through a letter or other form of support from the Nation).
Initiative advances the goals of 30x30 through durable conservation designations that meet IUCN standards for Protected Areas and Other Effective Conservation Measures (OECMs).
Formal conservation designations have to have occurred after April 1, 2024, and cannot have already been officially counted towards 30x30 targets.
government teams may not directly apply for funding to support their initiatives or studies.
Initiative aligns with a government-to-government agreement related to land use to guide investments.
Initiative supports the ongoing, stewardship of the area
Initiative provides meaningful biological, ecological, and cultural values and benefits and outcomes that are monitored over time
